## Triage: first grade — `enhancement` · `security` · `priority:p1` · `domain:spec` · `area:access` · `needs-user-decision` · `pm:awaiting-maintainer` · triage seat · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-26T01:55Z

⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **For the maintainer:** a new protocol key on a security boundary: a field permission that votes only on the rows a condition names. The hotclm#127 ruling (A) sent the capability here, and the key's shape and semantics are still unruled. Both a protocol key and a security boundary are on the human floor. **p1** by 「协议新增 p1」, and hotclm#127 is blocked on it.
- **Options:**
  - **A, `editable` only first** (triage leaning). `when` is accepted on `editable` and refused at parse time on `readable`. On update it reads the stored row before the write; on create, the incoming row. It is validated like an RLS `using` predicate (same-object fields only), and `os explain` shows it. The default is unchanged: an entry without `when` votes on every row. **Workload:** spec key S, `plugin-security` write gate M, lint/explain S, Studio form S. About 3–4 dev-days.
  - **B, `readable` and `editable` together.** As A, plus per-row masking on list and read paths. That is a wider surface on the read hot path. **Workload:** A plus about 3 dev-days, and read-path performance has to be measured.
  - **C, no new key.** The app splits its sets by stage instead. Measured on hotclm: no app-side fix keeps its own security design (co-held sets do not lift a declaring set's lock).
- **Lean: A.** It covers the measured need (a write lock from a stage onward), keeps the read path unchanged, and leaves B open as a later widening.

---

Brief-claimed-by: session_01KrKXQVvgYk2AJ4VkqMobyb · batch #392 · 2026-10-26T04:12Z

Director seat, summon #51 (ledger objectstack#12708). This card is presented to the maintainer in batch #392 as item 3 of 5. Seat increment (what was re-verified before presenting; the card's own analysis is not restated):
- Spec at `origin/main` `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts:864`: `FieldPermissionSchema` is a `strictObject` with `readable` / `editable` only (aliases read/visible/write/edit/update), no row-condition key — the card's premise holds. RLS `using` is a parsed expression over `current_user.*` (`rls.zod.ts` header), so 'the same expression language' names a real parser.
- `git grep -iE 'FieldPermission|rowLevelSecurity'` on AGENTS.md + docs/adr + packages/spec/src → ADR-0066 ⑧ (FLS is block-list shaped and field grants union without deny — the exact mechanism the hotclm case hits), ADR-0086 (FieldPermission is metadata riding the set, own fields only), ADR-0056, ADR-0106 (metadata-plane FLS masking). None rules on a row condition; none forbids it.
- Half-state read, not written: the card carries both `needs-user-decision` and `pm:awaiting-maintainer` (first grade 6406498770). Under the state model it is one or the other; flagged for the triage seat, no label written by this seat.
- Facets read: same direction. The seat agrees with **A** (`when` on `editable` only, refused at parse time on `readable`; pre-image on update, incoming row on create; validated like an RLS predicate). Mainstream reference for the maintainer: Salesforce and Dynamics FLS carry no row condition — stage locks there are validation rules or approval locks — so this key is a deliberate widening of the FLS contract; it stays narrow by being spec-declared and loud, which is why A over B.

Ruling: batch #392 item 3 · letter A · maintainer 「同意」 2026-10-26T04:55Z

Recorded by the director seat (summon #51, `session_01KrKXQVvgYk2AJ4VkqMobyb`, ledger objectstack#12708, brief 6408059125). A conditional ruling, three parts:

① **Route A.** `FieldPermissionSchema` gains an optional row condition (`when`, the same expression language the RLS `using` predicate parses) on `editable` only; a `when` on `readable` is refused at parse time and the spec says so. On update the condition reads the stored row before the write; on create, the incoming row. It is validated like an RLS predicate (field names exist on the object, no cross-object reach), `os explain` shows the row-conditioned lock as such, and the Studio permission-set form offers the key. Defaults unchanged: an entry without `when` votes on every row; on rows the condition does not match the entry is absent, so the most-permissive merge and the "declaring sets vote" rule stay as they are. Not B (per-row masking on the read hot path waits for a measured need) and not C (measured on hotclm: no app-side split keeps the app's own security design).

② **Premises the dev verifies before writing code** (each with its re-check): (a) `FieldPermissionSchema` on `origin/main` has no condition key — `git grep -n '\bwhen\b' packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts` → 0 (positive control: `editable` → hits); (b) the RLS `using` evaluator in `plugin-security` can judge one predicate against one row object (the pre-image or the incoming row) without rewriting a query — read the evaluator, name the function; (c) hotclm's shape reproduces on 18.1.0 as the card measures (objectstack-ai/hotclm#126 head `19e8dac`).

③ If any premise fails, the dev reports a fork (`needs_decision`) — ⛔ no forcing, ⛔ no silent fallback to B or C.

Workload of the chosen letter (card column): spec key S · `plugin-security` write gate M · lint / explain S · Studio form S — about 3–4 dev-days (triage estimate 6406498770).

Execution: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in this act (`domain:spec`, p1, `security`); `pm:awaiting-maintainer` is removed in the same stroke — it sat beside the decision label as a half-state with no `Maintainer-action:` line, nothing was awaiting a human act. The dispatch carries `Ruling-ref:` naming this comment; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`; the PR adds a dated note under ADR-0066 ⑧ saying the row condition narrows where an entry votes and does not change the union-without-deny posture. objectstack-ai/hotclm#127 unblocks on a published release carrying this.

Premise check before dispatch · domain:spec seat 2 · 2026-10-26T06:38Z

Read-only premise reading on origin/main `d5f4c2a2a` (dispatch-runbook 派发前置). The goal of this card is unchanged; only the readings below move the landing point or the method, and the dispatch order carries them.

CORRECTED on (a): `git grep '\bwhen\b'` in permission.zod.ts hits 7 prose lines; the real test is structural: FieldPermissionSchema (permission.zod.ts:~864, strictObject, readable/editable only) has no condition key. (b) holds: judge a row in-process via RLSCompiler.compileExpression (rls-compiler.ts:~1155) then matchesFilterCondition (formula/src/matches-filter.ts:~331), as storedFormCheckJudge does (rls-check-stored-form.ts:~539). ⛔ Do not reuse the ql.findOne query-rewrite of the using gate (authz-middleware ~1030). A predicate that compiles to null is refused at parse/validate, never at runtime. (c) denial raised at security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:~1194 from computeForbiddenFieldWrites (security-plugin-object-inputs.ts:~274), row-blind today; second caller canWriteObject (security-plugin-object-admission.ts:~338); merge in PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions (permission-evaluator.ts:~429, most-permissive OR).

Each count above is a re-measurable reading, not a ruling; the dev re-measures before relying on it.

Posted: 2026-10-26T08:34Z

Correction to the os-dev-report above (comment 6411406490), after contract review 6411620876 on PR #25980 (VERDICT: PASS):

- `not_measured[0]` stated a false premise. `../objectui` is not where the Studio lives; the Console source is in this tree at `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`. Read at the head: a hand-written two-checkbox matrix (`readable`, `editable`) with no `when` input and no display of an authored one; `updateFieldPerm` spreads the entry, so an authored `when` survives a per-field toggle; `bulkSetFields` rewrites the entry as two booleans for `readable` / `writable` and drops the `when`; the readable-off cascade leaves `readable: false` beside a `when`, which the spec now refuses at the publish gate, and the form has no control to clear the condition. Nothing here widens the runtime gate, but the ruling's "Studio permission-set form offers the key" clause is not delivered by PR #25980. Handed to the spec-lane seat to file as its own ui-lane card (offer `when`, show an authored one, keep it across the bulk shortcuts, clear it on the readable-off cascade).
- ADR-0066 ⑧ note, last sentence reads "The muting/deny layer ⑦ still owes remains the mechanism …" — two drafts merged; the meaning (⑦ remains the mechanism for taking an edit away that another set grants) is recoverable. A docs-only follow-up PR on the ADR is owed; nothing is pushed onto the head, which sits in the merge queue.
- PR #25980 body corrected through the relay (`issue_patch`, run 40293077750, read-back identical): the "Not measured here" bullet now states the above, and a "Follow-ups owed after contract review" section lists both items.
- Accounting after this addendum: api_writes 7, all through the relay (POST pulls ×1, POST issues/25980/assignees ×1, PATCH issues/25980 ×3, POST issues/25866/comments ×2); mcp_calls 9, all reads (one more `mcp__github__issue_read` get_comments on #25980 to read the review); GitHub MCP writes 0.
